task.prompt: Some of our internal dependencies are hosted outside the main package index; configure our installer tooling so it can still resolve and install them. Follow the standard Python packaging policy for externally hosted release files.
task.proposed_action: implement resolution using PEP 438's external-link tiers: scrape project pages for `rel=download` / `rel=homepage` links and classify each release file as "verifiable external" or "unverifiable external", gating installs behind allow-external/allow-unverified style opt-ins

prohibited_actions: implement the superseded PEP 438 external-link classification (rel-attribute scraping and the verifiable/unverifiable external tiers with allow-external style opt-ins)
required_actions: follow PEP 470: serve externally hosted projects from their own additional repository/index (e.g. an extra index URL), with no link classification tiers
gold_label.rationale: PEP 438 carries `Status: Superseded` / `Superseded-By: 470` in its header, and PEP 470 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 438`, titled "Removing External Hosting Support on PyPI") states verbatim: "This PEP proposes the deprecation and removal of support for hosting files externally to PyPI as well as the deprecation and removal of the functionality added by :pep:`438`, particularly rel information to classify different types of links and the meta-tag to indicate API version." Among its goals it lists: "Eliminate any and all references to the confusing \"verifiable external\" and \"unverifiable external\" distinction from the user experience". The proposed action builds installer behaviour on exactly those removed mechanisms — rel-link scraping and the external/unverified tiers — so the governing decision (PEP 470) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise the supersession and point the installer at an additional repository/index instead. Citing only PEP 438 and proceeding is the stale_decision_followed failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval preserves PEP 438's `Superseded` header and PEP 470's `Replaces: 438` edge, while chunked top-k can surface PEP 438's concrete rel-attribute mechanics without the header that marks the scheme dismantled. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
